proposed_widenings.name: vehicle_control_surface
proposed_widenings.justification: The item is a controllable vehicle/object with persistent internal state shared across repeated lever uses: legs extended/retracted, claws extended/retracted, shutters open/closed, hatch sealed/open, current movement mode, occupancy, and environmental constraints. The current magic-item families only cover passive grants, bounded activations, triggered reactions, summons, or composites of those; none model a pilot repeatedly operating a stateful vehicle.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature in the compartment can take a Utilize action to move as many as two of the apparatus's levers up or down. After each use, a lever goes back to its neutral position.

proposed_widenings.name: activation attachment: object_or_vehicle
proposed_widenings.justification: The existing activation surface can attach to self, target, area, or mark, but the apparatus's controls target the magic item itself as an object/vehicle. Several lever effects mutate the item's own state rather than the operator or another creature.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Legs extend, allowing the apparatus to walk and swim. Legs retract, reducing the apparatus's Speed and Swim Speed to 0 and making it unable to benefit from bonuses to speed.

proposed_widenings.name: persistent item mode/state gates
proposed_widenings.justification: Multiple lever outcomes are only legal or meaningful when a prior lever-established state is active, such as movement only when legs are extended and attacks only when claws are extended. The current surface has no way to author persistent item-state predicates or item-mode transitions that later activations depend on.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The apparatus walks or swims forward provided its legs are extended.

notes: No content file was authored. The item's core mechanics are a multi-control stateful vehicle, not a passive or bounded activation. A placeholder JSON would misrepresent the rules.
